members.name: Tiffany Zheng
members.bio: Tiffany, our President of Education, is a junior studying Computer Science and minoring in Operations Research and English. She has met her favorite author twice! Her favorite GWC memory is the Flower Knows event, where everyone bonded over a shared interest beyond code. Her advice for aspiring coders is to try everything at least twice, in coding and in life, because you never know if your first experience was just a bad one.

members.name: Keona Tang
members.bio: Keona, our President of Engagement, is a junior in SEAS studying Computer Science and minoring in Linguistics and Math. She joined GWC for its supportive, welcoming people and its commitment to giving back to the community. In her free time, she likes going to the gym and crocheting!

members.name: Hannah Kim
members.bio: Hannah, our VP of Education, is a junior studying Computer Science and minoring in Applied Math and Operations Research. She learned English by watching American sitcoms! Her favorite GWC memory is when a student stayed after the last class of the semester to ask about Columbia and careers in tech, a sign of the trusted mentorship they had built. Her advice for aspiring coders is to enjoy the failures, since each one is a valuable learning experience.

members.name: Prasie Gyenwali
members.bio: Prasie, our VP of Engagement, is a junior at Barnard studying Computer Science and minoring in Statistics and Psychology, with a particular interest in AI, system design, and building things end-to-end. On campus, she's involved in WiCS, Girls Who Code, SWE, ADI, and QuestBridge. When she's not coding, you'll probably find her exploring NYC, collecting trinkets and stickers, or hopping between cute cafes to yap with friends!

members.name: Grace Li
members.bio: Grace, our Secretary, is a junior studying Computer Science, Mathematics, and Dance. Born and raised in San Diego, she grew up as a competitive dancer and took a gap year before college to pursue professional ballet. This past summer, she was a software engineering intern at Square, and she has done research at Argonne National Laboratory, UChicago, and Columbia. Previously GWC's Internal Engagement Chair, she's excited to be Secretary this year!

members.name: Becca Frey
members.bio: Becca, our Treasurer, is a senior studying Computer Science and Math. She spent last semester studying abroad in London! Her favorite GWC memory is partnering with Flower Knows. Her advice for aspiring coders is that everyone starts somewhere, so keep trying and don't be afraid to ask for help.

members.name: Vrielle Guevarra
members.bio: Vrielle, our Curriculum Chair, is a sophomore studying Computer Science. She owns a pink Fender Strat guitar signed by beabadoobee and her bandmates! Her favorite GWC memory is painting flower pots at a committee bonding event. Her advice for aspiring coders is to embrace being a lifelong learner and stay curious and open-minded, because you never know what might interest you.

members.name: Laura Avila
members.bio: Laura, our Head Web Developer, is a junior studying Computer Engineering. She loves creating art, from oil painting to sketching with the Columbia Artist Society. Her favorite GWC memories are helping design the GWC website and making cute stickers for Activities Day. Her advice for aspiring coders is to try hackathons, because they aren't scary, and to start projects even if you don't feel ready, since that's exactly how you build new skills.

members.name: Ann Lee
members.bio: Ann, our Senior Advisor, is a senior studying computer science and math. Fun Fact: I like to crochet gifts for my friends! I also like to create illustrations in my free time :) Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: I love meeting students at our high school coding classes — it’s a great reminder of why I first got into computer science! Advice for (aspiring) coders: Use your coding skills to make things you like or things you would actually use!

members.name: Mimansa Kant
members.bio: Mimansa, our Senior Advisor, is a senior studying computer science and economics. Fun Fact: Black belt in taekwondo. Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Painting pumpkins at a G-boday event. Advice for (aspiring) coders: Try things even if they seem daunting, you never know what you might end up being interested in!

members.name: Hannah Kim
members.bio:
Hannah, our VP Internal, is a sophomore studying computer science and minoring applied math and operations research.

Fun fact: I learned English by watching American sitcoms! Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: When one of the students left behind after the last class of the semester to ask questions about Columbia and career in tech! I loved that we were able to build a trusted mentorship in class. Advice for (aspiring) coders: Try to enjoy the failures, since every one of them are a valuable learning experience!

members.name: Sreya Chakraborty
members.bio: Sreya, our VP External, is a sophomore studying computer science and economics.  Fun Fact: I can play the violin. Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Meeting a community of women in computer science through our various events and meetings. Advice for (aspiring) coders: My advice is to focus more on projects and applying your technical skills.

members.name: Natalie Mckenzie
members.bio: Natalie, our Treasurer, is a junior studying computer science and minoring in economics. Fun fact: I’ve logged over 1,000 hours on the Sims… Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Hosting the graduation for one of our classes! Being able to celebrate the students’ hard work with well-deserved food was really nice. Advice for (aspiring) coders: Ask questions like you paid for it (you did)!

members.name: Keona Tang
members.bio: Keona, our Secretary, is a sophomore studying computer science and minoring in math. Fun Fact: I have an extra bone in my foot! Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Tree lighting! It's always fun with friends :) Advice for (aspiring) coders: Don't be afraid to "rubber ducky" someone! Explaining your code step-by-step can really help you debug.

members.name: Prasie Gyenwali
members.bio: Prasie, our External Engagement Chair, is a sophomore studying Computer Science with a minor in Statistics. Fun fact: I own an impressive amount of Stitch (from Lilo & Stitch) merch even though I have never actually watched the movie. If you want the story, we will have to meet :) Favorite GWC/Columbia memory: I have been part of GWC since my freshman year of high school, so being in GWC at Columbia truly feels like home. One of my favorite moments was our Flower Knows event. Seeing so many girls come together and connect was really special. Advice for (aspiring) coders: Your brain literally gets better with practice. The more you show up and work through problems, the easier it becomes over time. Be patient, stay consistent, and trust the process. It will click.

members.name: Grace Li
members.bio: Grace, our Internal Engagement Chair, is a sophomore studying computer science and math.  Fun Fact: I'm a dancer! I dance with Columbia Repertory Ballet and Columbia Ballet Collaborative here at school. Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Frantically trying to get everything we needed for the April Fools event the night before haha. Advice for (aspiring) coders: Find a topic that interests you and start your own personal project!

members.name: Elizabeth Ting
members.bio: Elizabeth, our Curriculum Chair, is a senior studying computer science and minoring in economics. Fun Fact: I love collecting plants, especially succulents! Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Teaching my first class. I was super nervous, but my co-teachers were incredibly supportive, and the students were really engaged. It reminded me why I love teaching and being part of this community! Advice for (aspiring) coders: Stay curious and ask a lot of questions!

members.name: Tiffany Zheng
members.bio: Tiffany, our Co-Curriculum Chair, is a second-year studying computer science and minoring in operations research & English. Fun Fact: I’ve met my favorite author twice! Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Flower Knows Event!! It was so great to see everybody bond over another shared interest besides code. Advice for (aspiring) coders: try everything at least twice even in life; you never know if your first experience was just a bad one !!

members.name: Laura Avila
members.bio: Laura, our Head Web Developer, is a sophomore studying Computer Engineering. Fun fact: I love creating art, from oil painting to sketching with the Columbia Artist Society. Favorite memory at Columbia/GWC: Helping design the GWC website and creating cute stickers for Activities Day! Advice for aspiring coders: Don’t be afraid to try hackathons — they aren’t scary! And don’t feel like you don’t know enough to start a project, because starting projects is precisely how you build new skills.
